title: Rebind finite BIT tags and cutoff roles for the 679-owner control
body:
Rebuilds 36 call tables for the 679-owner control. Reused address 649 names a different owner and takes a two-factor target from grade 508 to 254, below 256. An analogous 451-factor legacy tag moves from the floor to half its value.

## Scope and source

Relates #7912 to #7911 and the inherited ternary catalogue. The chosen rank-4 × rank-3 paid leaf passes locally; a complete physical delivery to the changed target remains open. The complete source comparator is #7830 at `87fbf4f7b35b0f18ab12b5767775a9a424cf0b15`. The archive identifies additional inputs by exact commit, path and hash. Base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`; P104 toolkit #7852 `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212`.

## Reproduction

Extract `research/p104-bit679-finite-owner-binding/replay.tar.gz` into an empty directory. Check its inner checksum manifest. `python3 -I -B verify.py` verified tags, archive pins, the pair catalogue and mod 3/9/27 leaf controls, and rejected stale namespace and wrong owner controls. The archive preserves the verification evidence and controls. This is an offline research archive; hosted package execution is separate.

## Open next questions

Complete physical erasure, 451-factor cover, stock, precision and recovery before requalifying the supplier. The complete signed change is zero.

Clear1nsight prepared this result with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit DreamingOfClouds for the P104 toolkit and the predecessor authors identified in the archive. Related results: [P104 campaign board](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/7111#discussioncomment-19789228).
